nodes.title: Observed IP endpoint tuple
nodes.statement: A parsed IP packet yields source and destination addresses and a next-protocol identifier; a transport header can add ports when complete.
nodes.scope: network packet and flow structure, not release
nodes.limitations: The tuple is packet metadata, not authenticated identity or service approval.

nodes.title: Observed TCP header fields
nodes.statement: A complete TCP header supplies ports, sequence and acknowledgment fields, flags, and receive window for later state validation.
nodes.scope: network TCP packet context, not flow verdict
nodes.limitations: A single header cannot establish sequence validity or connection state.

nodes.title: Observed UDP header fields
nodes.statement: A complete UDP datagram header supplies source and destination ports, length, and checksum context.
nodes.scope: network UDP packet context, not session verdict
nodes.limitations: UDP has no connection state in its header; a port number is not an approved service.

nodes.title: Unreassembled fragment context
nodes.statement: A fragment identifies an original datagram and offset, while the complete transport header and checksum require reassembly context.
nodes.limitations: Fragment identity alone cannot be used as a full flow tuple.

nodes.title: Reassembled transport context
nodes.statement: Transport fields spanning fragments become attributable only after a complete, validated datagram is reassembled.
nodes.limitations: The current host path has no verified reassembly receipt; this node is not a claim that reassembly occurred.

nodes.title: TCP opening trace
nodes.statement: A connection opening is a sequence of correlated segments and sequence acknowledgments, not one SYN flag in isolation.
nodes.limitations: Peer identity and host policy remain separate inputs.

nodes.title: TCP sequence and window trace
nodes.statement: A later TCP segment is interpreted against prior sequence, acknowledgment, window, and payload-length state for that connection.
nodes.limitations: Raw sequence and ACK fields without prior state do not prove acceptable progression.

nodes.title: UDP reverse tuple observation
nodes.statement: A reverse-address and reverse-port UDP datagram can be correlated with an earlier datagram as a candidate response context.
nodes.limitations: A reversed tuple does not prove causation, identity, service approval, or a bounded response window.

nodes.title: IPv4 ICMP echo correspondence
nodes.statement: An IPv4 echo reply can be related to a request by reversed endpoints and matching identifier and sequence fields.
nodes.limitations: A matching pair is not host authorization; IPv6 echo is not represented by the current observer.

nodes.title: Current host service rule context
nodes.statement: A host firewall rule relates direction, endpoint, address range, protocol, and service to the current policy version.
nodes.limitations: The scratch node does not yet supply a versioned approved-service configuration.

nodes.title: Observed flow plus host context
nodes.statement: A host can combine a measured packet tuple and progression with the applicable current service rule before its own release decision.
nodes.limitations: The Lightcone records these prerequisites but does not evaluate or release the packet.

nodes.title: Unrepresented transport observation
nodes.statement: A structurally bounded IP packet with an unsupported upper-layer protocol has no claimed transport-flow relation in this revision.
nodes.limitations: A later version may source and represent the protocol; current absence is scoped, not universal.

nodes.title: Packet structure is not flow permission
nodes.statement: Parsed headers and a graph neighborhood cannot by themselves establish a permitted service, peer identity, or valid flow history.
nodes.limitations: Positive release requires a separately owned host policy decision with current context.

edges.conditions: An IPv4 or IPv6 header is completely validated.
edges.exceptions: A malformed or truncated header supplies no tuple.
edges.evidence: IP headers carry source and destination addresses.

edges.conditions: The complete TCP header follows a validated IP packet.
edges.exceptions: Fragments without reassembly do not establish TCP ports.
edges.evidence: TCP header fields include source and destination ports.

edges.conditions: The IP next-protocol field selects TCP and its full header is present.
edges.exceptions: Other upper-layer protocols use different tuple fields.
edges.evidence: A TCP flow tuple includes transport ports from the TCP header.

edges.conditions: The IP next-protocol field selects UDP and its full header is present.
edges.exceptions: Other upper-layer protocols use different tuple fields.
edges.evidence: A UDP tuple includes the datagram's source and destination ports.

edges.conditions: IPv4 fragment offset or more-fragments flag is present.
edges.exceptions: Unfragmented packets retain their complete transport header.
edges.evidence: Fragment offset and identification describe pieces of one datagram.

edges.conditions: The complete transport header has not been reassembled.
edges.exceptions: A verified reassembly owner may later supply a full packet.
edges.evidence: A later fragment need not carry TCP ports or sequence fields.

edges.conditions: All fragments are attributed to one datagram and the result is validated.
edges.exceptions: Lone, overlapping, or timed-out fragments remain incomplete.
edges.evidence: Transport interpretation follows reconstruction of fragmented IP payload.

edges.conditions: A correlated opening segment is observed for this tuple.
edges.exceptions: An isolated SYN flag is not a complete connection.
edges.evidence: TCP opening begins with sequence synchronization.

edges.conditions: Acknowledgment corresponds to the opening sequence state.
edges.exceptions: Orphan or stale ACKs are not opening progression.
edges.evidence: Acknowledgment advances the opening exchange.

edges.conditions: A bounded host flow owner records the correlated segment history.
edges.exceptions: The packet observer alone has no connection state.
edges.evidence: TCP segment effects depend on connection state.

edges.conditions: UDP length matches the validated datagram boundary.
edges.exceptions: A truncated datagram does not supply a complete header.
edges.evidence: UDP carries an explicit length field.

edges.conditions: Only a UDP header has been observed.
edges.exceptions: A host application can separately track its own UDP exchange.
edges.evidence: UDP header structure does not implement TCP connection state.

edges.conditions: A current versioned host rule names service and direction.
edges.exceptions: No configured rule means no approved-service fact can be asserted.
edges.evidence: Firewall policy enumerates necessary permitted services.

edges.conditions: A current outbound rule names applicable addresses and protocol.
edges.exceptions: A protocol name alone does not establish endpoint permission.
edges.evidence: Outbound policy constrains destination and service.

edges.conditions: Only packet header fields are available.
edges.exceptions: A host can add current policy and state before its own decision.
edges.evidence: A tuple is necessary context but not an authorization verdict.

edges.conditions: Packet structure is mistaken for a current host policy result.
edges.exceptions: A separate host decision may use packet structure as one input.
edges.evidence: The graph preserves the packet-policy boundary explicitly.

edges.conditions: An IPv4 echo request with identifier and sequence is recorded.
edges.exceptions: An unmatched reply has no request correspondence.
edges.evidence: The request supplies the identifier and sequence context.

edges.conditions: An IPv4 reply reverses endpoints and matches identifier and sequence.
edges.exceptions: A mismatched value is not the same request/reply pair.
edges.evidence: Echo replies return the request's identifier and sequence.

edges.conditions: The host holds the prior request while correlating the reply.
edges.exceptions: A single packet cannot prove prior request state.
edges.evidence: A matching pair is a temporal relation across two observations.

edges.conditions: The host has previous sequence progression for this tuple.
edges.exceptions: An arbitrary sequence value is not validated by a packet header alone.
edges.evidence: TCP sequence space orders bytes across segments.

edges.conditions: The current receive window and segment length are known.
edges.exceptions: Without payload/header lengths the segment advance is unresolved.
edges.evidence: Acceptability of a segment depends on sequence and window context.

edges.conditions: The segment belongs to the tracked connection state.
edges.exceptions: Orphan ACKs are not stateful progression.
edges.evidence: Sequence and acknowledgment handling is state dependent.

edges.conditions: A host records datagrams with swapped addresses and ports.
edges.exceptions: No response causation follows from the swap alone.
edges.evidence: UDP ports and IP addresses permit tuple comparison.

edges.conditions: Only the reverse tuple is known.
edges.exceptions: Current host policy and bounded exchange context may later support a decision.
edges.evidence: UDP has no built-in connection or service-approval state.

edges.conditions: The upper-layer protocol is not represented in this version.
edges.exceptions: A later sourced revision may add that mechanism.
edges.evidence: The packet header can name a protocol without supplying its causal model.

edges.conditions: No represented transport mechanism or approved service rule matches.
edges.exceptions: The host may separately define a later supported case.
edges.evidence: Unknown mechanism context cannot be silently promoted to a known flow.

edges.conditions: The host independently validated the current policy version, both zones and endpoints, service, direction, and bounded progression for this exact flow.
edges.exceptions: Graph reachability and a passive receipt do not release traffic without those host facts and a separate host decision.
edges.evidence: A permitted flow is specific to observed communication and current policy.

edges.conditions: The host independently validated the exact packet endpoints and protocol progression and bound them to this request.
edges.exceptions: A stale, mismatched, or header-only tuple cannot be substituted for current flow state.
edges.evidence: Host policy evaluates the observed source, destination, protocol, and service.

edges.conditions: The host authenticated a current policy rule naming both zones, service, and direction for this flow.
edges.exceptions: Missing, stale, or inapplicable policy supplies no approved-service context.
edges.evidence: The host decision must use the current declared rule.

edges.conditions: A fragment has no verified complete transport datagram.
edges.exceptions: A separate validated reassembly receipt can restore transport context.
edges.evidence: Incomplete fragments cannot supply all flow fields.

edges.conditions: The host has accepted all fragments into one complete datagram.
edges.exceptions: Missing, overlapping, or expired fragments prevent this relation.
edges.evidence: Reassembly resolves the incomplete fragment context.

controls.pair: same IPv4 UDP shape, declared versus undeclared destination service
controls.expected: graph structure may match; host policy must distinguish; no packet-only authorization

controls.pair: same TCP ACK shape, valid progression versus orphan or out-of-window ACK
controls.expected: raw headers alone cannot establish progression; prior state required

controls.pair: matching versus mismatched IPv4 echo identifier or sequence
controls.expected: only matched reverse endpoints and identifier/sequence form correspondence

controls.pair: represented IPv4 UDP versus unrepresented upper-layer protocol
controls.expected: unsupported protocol remains an explicit unknown, with no borrowed UDP relation

controls.pair: identical UDP headers with benign versus hostile payload text
controls.expected: payload text does not change structural mechanism or authorize a flow

controls.pair: complete unfragmented packet versus a lone unreassembled fragment
controls.expected: fragment identity is recorded but no complete transport tuple is inferred

controls.pair: positive graph path from observed tuple to authorized_flow with all host facts absent versus the same path with independently validated current host policy and progression
controls.expected: graph reachability alone never releases traffic; the host must validate every required fact before its own decision
